summary:
This joint resolution (H.J. Res. 133, enacted as Public Law 119-46, approved December 2, 2025) is a non-binding expression of congressional sentiment requesting executive action in connection with the commemoration of the 250th anniversary (semiquincentennial) of the founding of the United States. It carries no operative statutory command, does not amend the U.S. Code, and contains no authorization or appropriation of funds.

The resolution's single resolving clause performs two functions. First, in paragraph (1), Congress "requests"—it does not direct or mandate—that the Secretary of the Interior authorize "unique and one-time arrangements" for the display of United States semiquincentennial materials and other significant artifacts, digital content, film footage, and associated audio and imagery in and around the vicinity of the National Mall. The requested arrangements expressly include projection onto the surface of the Washington Monument for five nights of public display. The requested display period is temporally bounded, beginning December 31, 2025, and ending January 5, 2026.

Second, in paragraph (2), the resolution respectfully requests that the Clerk of the House of Representatives transmit an enrolled copy of the resolution to (A) the Secretary of the Interior and (B) the Chair of the United States Semiquincentennial Commission.

The extensive preambulatory (whereas) clauses provide historical context, referencing the adoption of the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776; the forthcoming July 4, 2026 anniversary; the United States Semiquincentennial Commission Act of 2016 (36 U.S.C. note prec. 101; Public Law 114-196), which established the Commission to plan and coordinate the commemoration; the 1976 bicentennial-era exploration of illuminating the Washington Monument and other capital monuments; and the 2019 Apollo 11 50th-anniversary commemoration on the National Mall, which included projection of program footage onto the Washington Monument. These recitals are non-operative and confer no legal authority.

Because the instrument is framed entirely as a request, it establishes no conditions precedent, imposes no deadlines binding on the Secretary, and confers no new authority beyond expressing the sense of Congress; any authorization for the described displays would rest on the Secretary of the Interior's existing statutory and regulatory authority over the National Mall and Washington Monument. The resolution's only date-specific terms are the requested December 31, 2025–January 5, 2026 display window and the enactment date of December 2, 2025.

Legislative history: passed the House November 18, 2025, and the Senate November 20, 2025 (Cong. Rec. Vol. 171 (2025)).
